plan.text:
Based on the BART Discounts page (https://www.bart.gov/tickets/discounts), here are the youth discount details:

**Ages that qualify for the youth discount:** 5-18 years old
**Discount amount:** 50% off
**Card required:** Youth Clipper card
**Children who ride free:** 4 years and younger

**Official source link:** https://www.bart.gov/tickets/discounts

Additional note: Youth and Senior Clipper cards can be obtained by mail or at multiple locations across the Bay Area where applicants will need to bring documentation verifying age eligibility (driver's license, photo ID card, or birth certificate).

Based on the official SFJAZZ ticket policies page, here are the details for returning tickets:

**Flat fee:** $25 flat fee for ticket returns purchased for SFJAZZ concerts (to receive Box Office Credit for a future concert)

**Advance-notice deadline:** Ticket returns are accepted up to 48 hours prior to the performance.

**Membership level that waives the fee:** The Contributor level ($250/year) and above.

**Official source link:** https://www.sfjazz.org/tickets/ticket-policies/

Based on the SFJAZZ ticket policies page:

- **Flat fee for returning tickets:** $25 (for Box Office Credit)
- **Advance-notice deadline:** Up to 48 hours prior to the performance
- **Membership level that waives the fee:** Contributor level ($250/year) and above

**Official source link:** https://www.sfjazz.org/tickets/ticket-policies/

The page states: "We charge a $25 flat fee for ticket returns purchased for SFJAZZ concerts, which allows a patron to receive ‘Box Office Credit’ for purchasing tickets to a future concert. This fee is waived for all members at the Contributor level ($250/year) and above." And: "Ticket returns are accepted up to 48 hours prior to the performance."

Note: You mentioned "return my tickets for credit" but I cannot actually process or return your tickets as I'm an AI assistant without access to your account. You would need to contact the Box Office at 415.788.7353 or log into your account to initiate a ticket return.

scope: Retain validated browser clarifications independently of transient history; qualify native planning candidates without replacing sufficient MCP capabilities.
policy: macOS MCP/native capabilities first. Context, schema, intent, evidence and completion defects do not establish a visual capability gap.
One build/test/inference at a time, jobs1, parallel tests off. No source edits during active builds/tests.

12 GB whole-Mac target; model probes use one authenticated loopback worker, two threads, 16K context and a sampled 4 GiB worker stop cap. This does not qualify whole-Mac RAM, instantaneous peaks or sustained heat.
No purchases, messages, real account changes, provider/phone actions, installed-host replacement, push or release.
findings: The browser Session already retained ComputerUseUnresolvedTextGoal after validated clarification transfer, but both Input constructions supplied only the original goal and transient/history answers. The MCP planner and completion guard therefore lacked an independent complete user-turn input.

The repair passes the existing typed goal through initial and loaded browser inputs, validates its exact UTF-8 root and browser surface, and supplies ordered question/answer context independently of history. Only user turns contribute user URL candidates. Questions and page/model records are interpretation data, not user authority.

The MCP completion boundary now applies its existing conservative guard to every accepted user turn. This does not solve semantic intent, cross-turn ambiguity, negation, unknown mutations or actual effect verification. Its known prohibition false positive remains open.

Fara request serialization includes exact retained clarification pairs in the current observation with their trust distinction, within existing text/body bounds. No model selection change or additional worker is introduced. Holo-specific serialization and actual-model quality are not newly qualified.
Qwen3.5 non-thinking and Agents-A1 non-thinking both report policy as an answer while a requested ticket return remains unperformed. Moving the exact goal after context does not fix Agents-A1.

Thinking Qwen recognizes the requested return but truncates at 1024 tokens. At 1536 it returns incomplete for return/purchase, then times out on release. Its return explanation incorrectly assigns the donation account portal to box-office-credit returns. No candidate is promoted.

Agents-A1 native function calls parse successfully through pinned b9992 after bounded ancillary narration is discarded. Its completeTask call still reports success with an explicit disclaimer that it cannot return tickets. Native protocol compatibility does not establish task correctness.

Three Apple intent diagnostics fail under distinct schemas. Intent plus actionQuote violates the quote contract on case1; intent alone mislabels requested return on case2; assessment before intent handles return/purchase but mislabels ordinary BART navigation on case4. The classifier is not installed, and its opt-in method was removed after preserving all three source snapshots.

The native-protocol Python prototype has executed RED/GREEN evidence for native calls and ancillary narration. Its final four methods cover malformed/duplicate/multiple/truncated/unknown calls and unchanged input without oracle leakage. No production native-function adapter was added.

Model expected kinds and fact regexes remain outside prompts. They do not fully score relevance, condition/subject association, semantic completeness, real Mac-tool capability gaps, Swift host integration, live website task success or 12 GB whole-Mac acceptance.

The first twelve-method app regression batch exposes two stale composition assertions: native observed_page text was added previously by 713e29b, but the expected URL/answer string omitted it. Updated assertions independently check native source/text/omission flags plus exact clarification pairs; task result and effect-count assertions remain.
General public/mixed/native workflows, normal HostSession, physical phone and real-provider login/handoff remain unaccepted. Main-thread responsiveness warnings remain open.

browserClarificationRetention.tested: Executed missing-clarifications RED, four-method GREEN, then twelve-method final regression batch with no failures or skips. First broader batch's two stale observed-page assertions are retained.
browserClarificationRetention.accepted: Scoped task input, exactness, ownership and continuation mechanics only.

nativeCompletionAdmission.tested: Accepted later purchase request blocks success; a question alone cannot introduce the request; incomplete remains failure.
nativeCompletionAdmission.accepted: Existing narrow guard applied to retained user turns, not general intent or effect proof.

candidateModels.compiled: Actual pinned b9992 model load; Python prototype tests
candidateModels.tested: Eight stopped model runs, three stopped Apple intent variants

controlledMCPHost.tested: Actual Apple planner and installed MCP helper through default HostComputerUseManager and production browser loader: complete result in 14.6057 seconds; one visit per page; zero installs, visual launch attempts or workers.
controlledMCPHost.accepted: Controlled informational workflow only; isolated transport/ledger/browser, not normal HostSession or real provider/phone qualification.

researchLimits: Agents-A1's author 4B card motivates an agent/tool experiment; the family paper's larger-model results do not establish 4B superiority or Mac specialty. Exact pinned templates were used, with explicit system prompts replacing Agents' stale default date. Optional generation_config files were absent at pinned revisions. Full model success, Mac specialty and Fara/Holo replacement remain unproven.
